chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v01] It is said that the secret of the Trika scripture is the differentiation of the tattvas.

[tal-a10-v10] By conditions beginning with knower and knowing, not produced by stain; but by knowers from sakala to Shiva, its knowability is that which...

[tal-a10-v02] The further difference among those tattvas, following in their own classes, is also declared in the scripture called Sri Trika.

[tal-a10-v03] By the difference of shaktiman and shakti, the range from earth to the root last is divided into fifteen by its own nature along with anara.

[tal-a10-v04] Up to kala, with two differences omitted, pralayakala is rudra-like; similarly maya is ninefold, and jnakala is sevenfold again.

[tal-a10-v05] Mantras are those lords in fivefold, mantra-lords are threefold, but Shiva is not divided, being one light-dense consciousness.

[tal-a10-v06] Shiva, mantra, mahesha, isha, mantra, akala, yuk, and kali are named; there are seven shaktimans and likewise fourteen shaktis.

[tal-a10-v07] Its own nature is the fifteenth; that ground is fifteenth-natured, for the three powers of the Lord were described before.

[tal-a10-v08] Those very powers are established in the threefold form of knower, knowing, and known; the supreme part is knower-form here, and the instrument part is intermediate.

[tal-a10-v09] The known is supreme; the power-holder part and power are its own nature; thus there the nature of the ground is that which stands separately as inert.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-:C10 atha śrītantrāloke daśamamāhnikam ucyate trikaśāstrekarahasyaṃ tattvabhedanam teṣāmamīṣāṃ tattvānāṃ svavargeṣvanugāminām / bhedāntaramapi proktaṃ śāstre@tra śrītrikābhidhe śaktimacchaktibhedena dharādyaṃ mūlapaścimam / bhidyate pañcadaśadhā svarūpeṇa sahānarāt kalāntaṃ bhedayugghīnaṃ rudravatpralayākalaḥ / tadvanmāyā ca navadhā jñākalāḥ saptadhā punaḥ mantrāstadīśāḥ pāñcadhye mantreśapatayastridhā / śivo na bhidyate svaikaprakāśaghanacinmayaḥ śivo mantramaheśeśamantrā akalayukkalī / śaktimantaḥ sapta tathā śaktayastaccaturdaśa svaṃ svarūpaṃ pañcadaśaṃ tadbhūḥ pañcadaśātmikā / tathāhi tisro devasya śaktayo varṇitāḥ purā tā eva mātṛmāmeyatrairūpyeṇa vyavasthitāḥ / parāṃśo mātṛrūpo@tra pramāṇāṃśaḥ parāparaḥ meyo@paraḥ śaktimāṃśca śaktiḥ svaṃ rūpamityadaḥ / tatra svarūpaṃ bhūmeryatpṛthagjaḍamavasthitam mātṛmānādyupadhibhirasaṃjātoparāgakam / sakalādiśivāntaistu mātṛbhirvedyatāsya yā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v11] By power-holders with unmanifest powers, seven divisions of those; from sakala to Shiva, in powers with raised self.

[tal-a10-v12] Knowability-born seven divisions; thus fourteen; of sakala, the instrument part which is vidya-kala-natured.

[tal-a10-v13] That generic-natured portion is counted in power, not as distinct from it; layakala's measure-portion is that same generic, most clear.

[tal-a10-v14] But jnanakala's measure is the melting vidyakala-covering, joined with the impression of destroyed impure-knowledge activity.

[tal-a10-v15] Yearning to awake, pure knowledge becomes the saviors' instrument; awakened, pure knowledge is joined with its own refinement.

[tal-a10-v16] The mantra-lords' measure is devoid of that impression; the mantra-great-lords' measure is called power as instrument.

[tal-a10-v17] The divine will-power, existing by mere freedom — that same is Shiva's instrument; by her he knows and he acts.

[tal-a10-v18] The seven measurers from Shiva to sakala are twofold; by diminished or excessive power, their division differentiates the perceptible.

[tal-a10-v19] Thus: perceptibility named is only the entity's own body — 'I know the perceptible through Caitra' — so what appears here?

[tal-a10-v20] Surely here only Caitra-cognition shines; perceptibility so-called does not shine as the entity's property the way blue does.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-śaktimadbhiranudbhūtaśaktibhiḥ sapta tadbhidaḥ / sakalādiśivāntānāṃ śaktiṣūdrecitātmasu vedyatājanitāḥ sapta bhedā iti caturdaśa / sakalasya pramāṇāṃśo yo@sau vidyākalātmakaḥ sāmānyātmā sa śaktitve gaṇito natu tadbhidaḥ / layākalasya mānāṃśaḥ sa eva paramasphuṭaḥ jñānākalasya mānaṃ tu galadvidyākalāvṛti / aśuddhavidyākalanādhvaṃsasaṃskārasaṃgatā prabubhutsuḥ śuddhavidyā santrāṇāṃ karaṇaṃ bhavet / prabuddhā śuddhavidyā tu tatsaṃskāreṇa saṃgatā mānaṃ mantreśvarāṇāṃ syāttatsaṃskāravivarjitā / mānaṃ mantramaheśānāṃ karaṇaṃ śaktirucyate svātantryamātrasadbhāvā yā tvicchā śaktiraiśvarī / śivasya saiva karaṇaṃ tayā vetti karoti ca ā śivātsakalāntaṃ ye mātāraḥ sapta te dvidhā / nyagbhūtodriktaśaktitvāttadbhedo vedyabhedakaḥ tathāhi vedyatā nāma bhāvasyaiva nijaṃ vapuḥ / caitreṇa vedyaṃ vedmīti kiṃhyatra pratibhāsatām nanu caitrīyavijñānamātramatra prakāśate / vedyatākhyastu no dharmo bhāti bhāvasya nīlavat

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v21] And if perceptibility were the entity's property by nature, then everything would be perceptible to all, like pot, blue and the rest.

[tal-a10-v22] Now, though the entity bears perceptibility through perceiver-awareness force, that too is defective — like weaver-made cloth.

[tal-a10-v23] But if that so-called perceptibility-property is itself unperceived, it is like a sky-flower; if it exists as perceived, there too is regress upon perceptibility.

[tal-a10-v24] Then nothing would be perceptible, and the world would be stupefied — but, you say, let the body be declared as fashioned by the cognizer's conditioning.

[tal-a10-v25] As this knowledge, whose nature is the entity's meaning-manifestation, is unreal — under single-knower knowability there is no knowability by another knower.

[tal-a10-v26] Under all-knower knowability there is no single-knower knowability — therefore perceptibility so-called is no entity's property at all.

[tal-a10-v27] The entity's perceptibility is just that uprising of consciousness whose form is object-grasping, where awareness stands in itself.

[tal-a10-v28] The manifest object unites with it — counter to that stands this very perceptibility. Here we say: if perceptibility is no property of objects...

[tal-a10-v29] They would indeed be unknowable even when knowledge is truly described — as with the pot of broad-based form, even though it is real.

[tal-a10-v30] Cloth, not having that nature, does not take on broad-based form — so too, though knowledge exists conjoined with the knower.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-vedyatā ca svabhāvena dharmo bhāvasya cettataḥ / sarvānpratyeva vedyaḥ syāddhaṭanīlādidharmavat atha vedakasaṃvittibalādvedyatvadharmabhāk / bhāvastathāpi doṣo@sau kuvindakṛtavastravat vedyatākhyastu yo dharmaḥ so@vedyaścetkhapuṣpavat / vedyaścedasti tatrāpi vedyetatyanavasthitiḥ tato na kiṃcidvedyaṃ syānmūrchitaṃ tu jagadbhavet / nanu vijñātrupādhyaṃ śo paskṛtaṃ vapurucyatām bhāvasyārthaprakāśātma yathā jñānamidaṃ tvasat / ekavijñātṛvedyatve na jñātrantaravedyatā samastajñātṛvedyatve naikavijñātṛvedyatā / tasmānna vedyatā nāma bhāvadharmo@sti kaścana bhāvasya vedyatā saiva saṃvido yaḥ samudbhavaḥ / arthagrahaṇarūpaṃ hi yatra vijñānamātmani samavaiti prakāśyo@rthastaṃ pratyeṣaiva vedyatā / atra brūmaḥ padārthānāṃ na dharmo yadi vedyatā avedyā eva te saṃsyurjñāne satyapi varṇite / yathāhi pṛthubudhnādirūpe kumbhasya satyapi atadātmā paṭo naiti pṛthubudhnādirūpatām / tathā satyapi vijñāne vijñātṛsamavāyini

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v31] How would unperceptible-natured entities attain perceptibility? This is a very great absurdity — look at the entity itself.

[tal-a10-v32] Not light-natured is that consciousness — unlit, resting on that; unlit are mind, lamp, eye and the rest — and just so is that.

[tal-a10-v33] What is called being its light when the world sleeps on every side? Surely knowledge's object-illumination has lamp-form.

[tal-a10-v34] Nothing unprecedented is known here, and we perform no woman-dance — therefore let it be stated what form knowledge's object-illumination has.

[tal-a10-v35] If the object is light — is the object the form, or knowledge itself? Now, whatever illumination of the object there is, that is called its form.

[tal-a10-v36] If the sixth is stated in the agent sense, the defect is hard to remove; now, this sixth in the object sense — the making-force stands firm at heart.

[tal-a10-v37] And so we show this: what, does light shine? That thing is not without light either — and so nothing at all is.

[tal-a10-v38] Then how is causal sense spoken of in the world when what abides is conscious? Its primary field is among the inert; toward consciousness it is only figurative.

[tal-a10-v39] Thus though Caitra is able to go, taking the going as dependent on another, thinking so he speaks: I am gone, master.

[tal-a10-v40] The master too, knowing the power in that going, seeing dependence plainly and fearing the stop, speaks: I shall make him go.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-avedyadharmakā bhāvāḥ kathaṃ vedyatvamāpnuyuḥ / anarthaḥ sumahāṃścaiṣa dṛśyatāṃ vastu yatsvayam prakāśātma na tatsaṃviccāprakāśā tadāśrayaḥ / aprakāśo manodīpacakṣurādi tathaiva tat kiṃ tatprakāśatāṃ nāma supte jagati sarvataḥ / jñānasyārthaprakāśatvaṃ nanu rūpaṃ pradīpavat apūrvamatra viditaṃ narīnṛtyāmahe tataḥ / arthaprakāśo jñānasya yadrūpaṃ tannirūpyatām arthaḥ prakāśaścedrūpamartho vā jñānameva vā / athārthasya prakāśo yastadrūpamiti bhaṇyate ṣaṣṭhī kartari cedukto doṣa eva duruddharaḥ / atha karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhyeṣā ṇyarthastatra hṛdi sthitaḥ tathā cedaṃ darśayāmaḥ kiṃ prakāśaḥ prakāśate / aprakāśo@pi naivāsau tathāpi ca na kiṃcana tarhi loke kathaṃ ṇyarthaḥ ucyate cetanasthitau / mukhyo ṇyarthasya viṣayo jaḍeṣu tvaupacārikaḥ tathāhi gantuṃ śakto@pi caitro@nyāyattatāṃ gateḥ / manvāna eva vaktyasmi gamitaḥ svāmineti hi svāmyapyasya gatau śaktiṃ buddhvā svādhīnatāṃ sphuṭam / paśyannivṛttimāśaṃkya gamayāmīti bhāṣate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v41] Thus the causal connection is primary between the moved and the mover; another too, in the world, acts accordingly, from that intention.

[tal-a10-v42] Here, in the words he makes the arrow go, one who posits the operation named impetus, thinking it the mover — that mover arises by figuration alone.

[tal-a10-v43] Here wind throws mountain, but both are inert and imagined by seers as mover and moved.

[tal-a10-v44] Thus in relation with an inert thing, primary causal sense is not; let it be elsewhere, for I have spread this out in detail.

[tal-a10-v45] Manifestation in meaning is metaphor; let it be; if it shines, then that itself is like a falling mountain.

[tal-a10-v46] In metaphor, wind becomes by some cause; here 'throws mountain' has as cause an action done by that.

[tal-a10-v47] On the mountain, this attains fall from destruction of conjunction; but here knowledge of an object is not action at all.

[tal-a10-v48] How can metaphor indeed be? That too is an unmanifest thing; an unmanifested object is not manifested by metaphor of manifestation.

[tal-a10-v49] Just as a child is not burned by mere approach to fire, so approach alone lacks the seed of burning.

[tal-a10-v50] But where truth is established in consciousness, the approach of light has a fitting and clear seed.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-preryaprerakayorevaṃ maulikī ṇyarthasaṃgatiḥ / tadabhiprāyato@nyo@pi loke vyavaharettathā śaraṃ gamayatītyatra punarvegākhyasaṃskriyām / vidadhatprerakammanya upacāreṇa jāyate vāyuradriṃ pātayatītyatra dvāvapi tau jaḍau / draṣṭṛbhiḥ prerakapreryavapuṣā parikalpitau itthaṃ jaḍena saṃbandhe na mukhyā ṇyarthasaṃgatiḥ / āstāmanyatra vitatametadvistarato mayā arthe prakāśanā seyamupacārastato bhavet / astu cedbhāsate tarhi sa eva patadadrivat upacāre nimittena kenāpi kila bhūyate / vāyuḥ pātayatītyatra nimittaṃ tatkṛtā kriyā girau yenaiṣa saṃyoganāśādbhraṃśaṃ prapadyate / iha tu jñānamarthasya na kiṃcitkarameva tat upacāraḥ kathaṃ nāma bhavetso@pi hyavastusan / aprakāśita evārthaḥ prakāśatvopacārataḥ tādṛgeva śiśuḥ kiṃ hi dahatyagnyupacārataḥ / śiśau vahnyupacāre yadbījaṃ taikṣṇyādi tacca sat prakāśatvopacāre tu kiṃ bījaṃ yatra satyatā / siddhe hi cetane yukta upacāraḥ sa hi sphuṭam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v51] That superimposition-natured thing lives by reconnection; yet no conscious knowledge exists as such.

[tal-a10-v52] An unlit thing is lit by another; but how is a lamp the light of form?

[tal-a10-v53] Here too these reasoning contrivances do not carry; a lamp lights form by its own form.

[tal-a10-v54] Such knowledge shines by itself, but not so; this lamp gives beings abundant light.

[tal-a10-v55] Otherwise they would not shine; therefore this previously stated light is supreme Shiva.

[tal-a10-v56] As each thing-body shines clearly, so blueness, named, shines in some way.

[tal-a10-v57] Thus knowability shines; its fruit is the thing-part gone behind, and consciousness knows two.

[tal-a10-v58] Connection is protected from the opposite and mutual; thus a hidden thief is clearly knowable.

[tal-a10-v59] Having known, he did not take; though desire overcame him, she sees me respectfully with one third of an eye.

[tal-a10-v60] The lover sees his own body sprinkled with nectar; it is not merely knowledge-awareness, but the thing-part gone behind.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-adhyāropātmakaḥ so@pi pratisaṃdhānajīvitaḥ / na cādyāpi kimapyasti cetanaṃ jñānamapyadaḥ aprakāśaṃ tadanyena tatprakāśe@pyayaṃ vidhiḥ / nanu pradīpo rūpasya prakāśaḥ kathamīdṛśam atrāpi na vahantyetāḥ kiṃ nu yuktivikalpanāḥ / yādṛśā svena rūpeṇa dīpo rūpaṃ prakāśayet tādṛśā svayamapyeṣa bhāti jñānaṃ tu no tathā / pradīpaścaiṣa bhāvānāṃ prakāśatvaṃ dadā[dhā]tyalam anyathā na prakāśerannabhede cedṛśo vidhiḥ / tasmātprakāśa evāyaṃ pūrvoktaḥ paramaḥ śivaḥ yathā yathā prakāśeta tattadbhāvavapuḥ sphuṭam / evaṃ ca nīlatā nāma yathā kācitprakāśate tadvaccakāsti vedyatvaṃ tacca bhāvāṃśapṛṣṭhagam / phalaṃ prakaṭatārthasya saṃvidveti dvayaṃ tataḥ vipakṣato rakṣitaṃ ca saṃdhānaṃ cāpi tanmithaḥ / tathāhi nibhṛtaścauraścaitravedyamiti sphuṭam buddhvā nādatta evāśu parīpsāvivaśo@pi san / seyaṃ paśyati māṃ netratribhāgeneti sādaram svaṃ dehamamṛteneva siktaṃ paśyati kāmukaḥ / na caitajjñānasaṃvittimātraṃ bhāvāṃśapṛṣṭhagam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v61] If knowability is a quality of all things, one must ask what that quality itself is.

[tal-a10-v62] The opponent's claim undermines itself, unlike the self-luminous Shiva view.

[tal-a10-v63] Nothing merely shines toward another; the blue pot is known to all.

[tal-a10-v64] Dull minds grasp a view that is almost unknown, while blueness is perceived in Rudra's body.

[tal-a10-v65] Your blue thing is not yellow; blue is not merely toward someone.

[tal-a10-v66] Knowability would be gated by imagination, contrary to accepted knowledge as object-light.

[tal-a10-v67] The opponent cannot state the form of knower-dependent knowability.

[tal-a10-v68] The knower of an object should be stated, and knowability shines toward all.

[tal-a10-v69] The objector would become a deaf bull, since knowability does not shine toward another.

[tal-a10-v70] When entity-form is stated, the opponent's rootless view is driven away by policy.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-arthakriyākaraṃ taccenna dharmaḥ konvasau bhavet / yaccoktaṃ vedyatādharmā bhāvaḥ sarvānapi prati syādityetatsvapakṣaghnaṃ duṣprayogāstravattava / asmākaṃ tu svaprakāśaśivatāmātravādinām anyaṃ prati cakāstīti vaca eva na vidyate / sarvānprati ca tannīlaṃ sa ghaṭaśceti yadvacaḥ tadapyaviditaprāyaṃ gṛhītaṃ mugdhabuddhibhiḥ / nahi kālāgnirudrīyakāyāvagatanīlimā tava nīlaḥ kiṃ nu pīto maivaṃ bhūnnatu nīlakaḥ / na kaṃcitprati nīlo@sau nīlo vā yaṃ prati sthitaḥ taṃ pratyeva sa vedyaḥ syātsaṃkalpadvārako@ntataḥ / yathā cārthaprakāśātma jñānaṃ saṃgīryate tvayā tathā tajjñātṛvedyatvaṃ bhāvīyaṃ rūpamucyatām / na ca jñātātra niyataḥ kaścijjñāne yathā tava arthe jñātā yadā yo yastadvedyaṃ vapurucyatām / tattadvijñātṛvedyatvaṃ sarvānpratyeva bhāsatām ityevaṃ codayanmanye vrajedbadhiradhuryatām / nahyanyaṃ prati vai kaṃcidbhāti sā vedyatā tathā bhāvasya rūpamityukte keyamasthānavaidhurī / anena nītimārgeṇa nirmūlamapasāritā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v71] Knowability is not a regress like blue; it is the quality that makes all qualities.

[tal-a10-v72] The qualified thing attains knowability, as existence inheres in being.

[tal-a10-v73] Conjunction, though joined, reaches a final distinction whose form is difference, excluding what is not different.

[tal-a10-v74] Whiteness moves between white and not-white, while the substrate itself stands endowed with blue and other qualities.

[tal-a10-v75] The unknowable gains knowability from knowable nature; knowability shines by itself, like blue and other qualities.

[tal-a10-v76] The unmanifest attains manifestness from self-manifest quality; indeed the universe takes rest in manifestation.

[tal-a10-v77] No other dependence is needed for the accomplished; as Shiva manifests difference by his own freedom.

[tal-a10-v78] Thus knowability is called a quality like blue; knowability of being is established, so what aversion?

[tal-a10-v79] But this must be considered: if knowability were uniform for all knowers, how could it be a fourteenth view?

[tal-a10-v80] It is said that if the being-related form is complete, that all-pervading Bhairava, the lord himself, is declared.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-anavasthā tathā hyanyairnīlādyaiḥ sadṛśī na sā / vedyatā kiṃtu dharmo@sau yadyogātsarvadharmavān dharmī vedyatvamabhyeti sa sattāsamavāyavat / brūṣe yathā hi kurute sattā satyasataḥ sataḥ samavāyo@pi saṃśliṣṭaḥ śliṣṭānaśliṣṭatājuṣaḥ / antyo viśeṣo vyāvṛttirūpo vyāvṛttivarjitān vyāvṛttān śvetimā śuklamaśuklaṃ gamanaṃ tathā / tadvannīlādidharmāṃśayukto dharmī svayaṃ sthitaḥ avedyo vedyatārūpāddharmādvedyatvamāgataḥ / vedyatā bhāsamānā ca svayaṃ nīlādidharmavat aprakāśā svaprakāśāddharmādeti prakāśatām / prakāśe khalu viśrāntiṃ viśvaṃ śrayati cettataḥ nānyā kācidapekṣāsya kṛtakṛtyasya sarvataḥ / yathā ca śivanāthena svātantryādbhāsyate bhidā nīlādivattathaivāyaṃ vedyatā dharma ucyate / evaṃ siddhaṃ hi vedyatvaṃ bhāvadharmo@stu kā ghṛṇā idaṃ tu cintyaṃ sakalaparyantoktapramātṛbhiḥ / vedyatvamekarūpaṃ syāccāturdaśyamataḥ kutaḥ ucyate paripūrṇaṃ cedbhāvīyaṃ rūpamucyate / tadvibhurbhairavo devo bhagavāneva bhaṇyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v81] Now if an imagined gradual partial glory is tolerated, what then is accomplished by this stated imagination?

[tal-a10-v82] Therefore, when it shines by a body, as it shines, then it is that form; this is the supreme upanishad.

[tal-a10-v83] Caitra knows the knowable by two, by many, by mantra, and by that great lord Shiva with exalted power.

[tal-a10-v84] Being shines as another kind; thus variety of action and so on arises without enumeration.

[tal-a10-v85] Thus the one-pointed whole assembly indeed considers dance and song as an ocean of nectar-essence.

[tal-a10-v86] From that it is said, in the instruction of watching wrestler-actor, the identity of all knowers reveals the full form.

[tal-a10-v87] If they are individually satisfied with cognition of that much meaning, what quality would their combined unity of knowers be?

[tal-a10-v88] But when that thing is pregnant with a cluster of knowable properties and endowed with something other than dry prior form, then...

[tal-a10-v89] In scripture too, knowability of each produces distinct purposeful action, and thus in the Shri Malinivijayottara.

[tal-a10-v90] Thus one should remember the sixfold path established by this; indeed the foundation by god is manifestation of which universe.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-atha tannijamāhātmyakalpitoṃ@śāṃśikākramaḥ / sahyate kiṃ kṛtaṃ tarhi proktakalpanayānayā ata eva yadā yena vapuṣā bhāti yadyathā / tadā tathā tattadrūpamityeṣopaniṣatparā caitreṇa vedyaṃ jānāmi dvābhyāṃ bahubhirapyatha / mantreṇa tanmaheśena śivenodriktaśaktinā anyādṛśena vetyevaṃ bhāvo bhāti yathā tathā / arthakriyādivaicitryamabhyetyaparisaṃkhyayā tathā hyekāgrasakalasāmājikajanaḥ khalu / nṛttaṃ gītaṃ sudhāsārasāgaratvena manyate tata evocyate mallanaṭaprekṣopadeśane / sarvapramātṛtādātmyaṃ pūrṇarūpānubhāvakam tāvanmātrārthasaṃvittituṣṭāḥ pratyekaśo yadi / kaḥ saṃbhūya guṇasteṣāṃ pramātraikyaṃ bhavecca kim yadā tu tattadvedyatvadharmasaṃdarbhagarbhitam / tadvastu śuṣkātprāgrūpādanyadyuktamidaṃ tadā śāstre@pi tattadvedyatvaṃ viśiṣṭārthakriyākaram / bhūyasaiva tathāca śrīmālinīvijayottare tathā ṣaḍvidhamadhvānamanenādhiṣṭhitaṃ smaret / adhiṣṭhānaṃ hi devena yadviśvasya pravedanam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v100] The ones named sakala-abode have all sheaths subdued; the knowledge-akalās have that sheath destroyed — thus the conclusion.

[tal-a10-v91] Thus knowability, called a property of being, is established and shines.

[tal-a10-v92] But in union with non-manifestation, own nature is said, clearly dispelling doubt of adjunct union.

[tal-a10-v93] By which form of one's own self the meaning shines, that own body; I know the pot here, endowed with knowability's coloring.

[tal-a10-v94] The pot indeed shone by its own form, it is declared; but there, is self-knowable being dependent on mantra and so on?

[tal-a10-v95] Also it indeed exists; let it be, but it does not appear; the unknowable indeed, of Meru having fire-body, supreme directions.

[tal-a10-v96] "Mine" in consciousness: the supreme pure thing shines; though knowable due to shining, not that, as knowable, from shining.

[tal-a10-v97] Indeed perception itself is imperceptible; in this way we inquire — this fifteen-aspected earth, and water and the like.

[tal-a10-v98] From their unmanifest-end, perceptibility toward sakala is said — endowed from kalā down to earth.

[tal-a10-v99] Sakala is so called by the excess of its six sheaths — the sheaths of arisen impure consciousness, attachment, kalā and the rest, of rasa.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tadīśavedyatvenetthaṃ jñātaṃ prakṛtakāryakṛt / evaṃ siddhaṃ vedyatākhyo dharmo bhāvasya bhāsate tadanābhāsayoge tu svarūpamiti bhaṇyate / upādhiyogitāśaṅkāmapahastayato@sphuṭam svātmano yena vapuṣā bhātyarthastatsvakaṃ vapuḥ / jānāmi ghaṭamityatra vedyatānuparāgavān ghaṭa eva svarūpeṇa bhāta ityapadiśyate / nanu tatra svayaṃvedyabhāvo mantrādyapekṣayā api cāstyeva nanvastu natu sanpratibhāsate / avedyameva kālāgnivapurmeroḥ parā diśaḥ mameti saṃvidi paraṃ śuddhaṃ vastu prakāśate / bhātatvādvedyamapi tanna vedyatvena bhāsanāt avedyameva bhānaṃ hi tathā kamanuyuñjmahe / evaṃ pañcadaśātmeyaṃ dharā tadvajjalādayaḥ avyaktāntā yato@styeṣāṃ sakalaṃ prati vedyatā / yattūcyate kalādyena dharāntena samanvitāḥ sakalā iti tatkośaṣaṭkodrekopalakṣaṇam / udbhūtāśuddhacidrāgakalādirasakañcukāḥ sakalālayasaṃjñāstu nyagbhūtākhilakañcukāḥ / jñānākalāstu dhvastaitatkañcukā iti nirṇayaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v101] Therefore even in pradhāna as object, the man with arisen sheath — the perceiver is indeed sakala, established according to the fifteen-aspect doctrine.

[tal-a10-v102] The fifteen-fold sakala, situated within earth to its end, even in sakala has an interior of sakala; even in the object of knowledge the knower is indeed.

[tal-a10-v103] The gross enveloped principles, yellow and so forth, number fourteen in earth and the other elements.

[tal-a10-v104] Inertness become own form, then knowerhood is declared as holding in the breath and body path in the Vijayottara.

[tal-a10-v105] When measurability is assumed for man, the arisen sheath portion is measurable, but that is not his knowerhood.

[tal-a10-v106] Therefore knowerhood does not exist for the all-named one; thirteen-ness remains after excluding the power and powered duality.

[tal-a10-v107] The subordinate sheath, mother, joined there with dissolution kala, and Maya-entered vijnanakala and others remain as before.

[tal-a10-v108] In the Maya principle's knowable form, even the subordinate sheath is measurable, because Maya is very subtle and unified with the sheath.

[tal-a10-v109] Indeed vijnanakala is here; then the mother sheath, even in Maya-entered kala, gives eleven-fold selfhood.

[tal-a10-v110] In pure vijnana, the knowable well established after sheath destruction, motherhood belongs to mantras desiring awakening.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tena pradhāne vedye@pi pumānudbhūtakañcukaḥ / pramātāstyeva sakalaḥ pāñcadaśyamataḥ sthitam pāñcadaśyaṃ dharādhantarniviṣṭe sakale@pi ca / sakalāntaramastyeva prameye@trāpi mātṛ hi sthūlāvṛtādisaṃkocatadanyavyāptṛtājuṣaḥ / pītādyāḥ sthirakampratvāccaturdaśa dharādiṣu svarūpībhūtajaḍatāḥ prāṇadehapathe tataḥ / pramātṛtājuṣaḥ proktā dhāraṇā vijayottare yadā tu meyatā puṃsaḥ kalāntasya prakalpyate / tadudbhūtaḥ kañcukāṃśo meyo nāsya pramātṛtā ataḥ sakalasaṃjñasya pramātṛtvaṃ na vidyate / trayodaśatvaṃ tacchaktiśaktimaddvayavarjanāt nyagbhūtakañcuko mātā yukta[yata]statra layākalaḥ / māyāniviṣṭo vijñānākalādyāḥ prāgvadeva tu māyātattve jñeyarūpe kañcukanyagbhavo@pi yaḥ / so@pi meyaḥ kañcukaikyaṃ yato māyā susūkṣmikā vijñānākala evātra tato mātāpakañcukaḥ / māyāniviṣṭe@pyakale tathetyekādaśātmatā vijñānakevale vedye kañcukadhvaṃsasusthite / udbubhūṣuprabodhānāṃ mantrāṇāmeva mātṛtā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v111] Even those mantras, when measurable, have their lord as mother; but when full awareness arises there, measurability is removed.

[tal-a10-v112] He of arisen full form is mother, the mantra great lord; when knowability is obtained there, supreme self-luminous Shiva appears.

[tal-a10-v113] The knower is Shiva, whose self-sameness illuminates all knowable; he is not measurable because illumination does not depend on another.

[tal-a10-v114] That measurability is not there, for he is the self-luminous lord; when no other is accepted in self-luminosity, measurability is absent.

[tal-a10-v115] A regress from non-luminous to luminous is insurmountable; otherwise the universe would remain asleep.

[tal-a10-v116] Since Shiva is self-luminous, other logical displays are unnecessary.

[tal-a10-v117] The supreme soul was said from the beginning; yet knowability is questioned even in self-luminous Shiva.

[tal-a10-v118] Otherwise instruction and teacherhood convention could not exist; truth is created thus by the supreme lord for knowability.

[tal-a10-v119] Led to the mantra-lord level, he is made to meditate; thus knowable, he is not unlimited consciousness.

[tal-a10-v120] Knowability is fitting for the full one, but in reality shiva-selfhood is not found in knowable nature.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-te@pi mantrā yadā meyāstadā mātā tadīśvaraḥ / sa hyudbhavātpūrṇabodhastasminprāpte tu meyatām udbhūtapūrṇarūpo@sau mātā mantramaheśvaraḥ / tasminvijñeyatāṃ prāpte svaprakāśaḥ paraḥ śivaḥ pramātā svakatādātmyabhāsitākhilavedyakaḥ / śivaḥ pramātā no meyo hyanyādhīnaprakāśatā meyatā sā na tatrāsti svaprakāśo hyasau prabhuḥ / svaprakāśe@tra kasmiṃścidanabhyupagate sati aprakāśātprakāśatve hyanavasthā duruttarā / tataśca suptaṃ viśvaṃ syānna caivaṃ bhāsate hi tat anyādhīnaprakāśaṃ hi tadbhātyanyastvasau śivaḥ / ityasya svaprakāśatve kimanyairyuktiḍambaraiḥ mānānāṃ hi paro jīvaḥ sa evetyuktamāditaḥ / nanvasti svaprakāśe@pi śive vedyatvamīdṛśaḥ upadeśo[śyo]padeṣṭṛtvavyavahāro@nyathā katham / satyaṃ sa tu tathā sṛṣṭaḥ parameśena vedyatām nīto mantramaheśādikakṣyāṃ samadhiśāyyate / tathābhūtaśca vedyo@sau nānavacchinnasaṃvidaḥ pūrṇasya vedyatā yuktā parasparavirodhataḥ / tathā vedyasvabhāve@pi vastuto na śivātmatām

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v121] Some state is relinquished so that meditation bears fruit; the glorious earlier scripture says it thus — Shiva is not divided in reality.

[tal-a10-v122] By the direct word the whole meaning is made clear; yet endowed with oneness, Shiva would depend on that alone.

[tal-a10-v123] What dispute is here in the great lord of the three-veda mantra — between the mantras of Maheśvara-īśa and the two kevalins?

[tal-a10-v124] Standing one by one from infinite differentiation, as with sakala indeed; then in the layakala, in the object, a perceiver exists — the layakala.

[tal-a10-v125] Therefore thirteen-foldness may hold — not eleven-fold selfhood; even in the perceptibility of the vijñānākala another might be a jñānākala.

[tal-a10-v126] Mother, that eleven-foldness would not be, nor nine-selfhood; thus it is in the arising of the interval between the mantras and their lords.

[tal-a10-v127] Although knowability yields nine, the seven and five are both asserted; the distinction is true and very clear.

[tal-a10-v128] As here in the whole there is difference, so it is not in the non-whole; the infinite interval and source difference make this clear.

[tal-a10-v129] The fourteen-fold whole has difference; in dissolution, though only impression remains, difference is still true.

[tal-a10-v130] The non-whole fits distinction for the whole; knowledge-only and similar states have no such difference.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ko@pi bhāvaḥ projjhatīti satyaṃ tadbhāvanā phalet / śrīpūrvaśāstre tenoktaṃ śivaḥ sākṣānna bhidyate sākṣātpadenāyamarthaḥ samastaḥ prasphuṭīkṛtaḥ / nanvekarūpatāyuktaḥ śivastadvaśato bhavet trivedatāmantramahānāthe kātra vivāditā / maheśvareśamantrāṇāṃ tathā kevalinordvayoḥ anantabhedataikaikaṃ sthitā sakalavatkila / tato layākale meye pramātāsti layākalaḥ atastrayodaśatvaṃ syāditthaṃ naikādaśātmatā / vijñānākalavedyatve@pyanyo jñānākalo bhavet mātā tadekādaśatā syānnaiva tu navātmatā / evaṃ mantratadīśānāṃ mantreśāntarasaṃbhave vedyatvānnava sapta syuḥ sapta pañca tu te katham / ucyate satyamastyeṣā kalanā kiṃtu susphuṭaḥ yathātra sakale bhedo na tathā tvakalādike / anantāvāntaredṛkṣayonibhedavataḥ sphuṭam caturdaśavidhasyāsya sakalasyāsti bheditā / layākale tu saṃskāramātrātsatyapyasau bhidā akalena viśeṣāya sakalasyaiva yujyate / vijñānakevalādīnāṃ tāvatyapi na vai bhidā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v131] Shiva's free will alone unfolds difference for these; seeing distinction, one views the whole and others here.

[tal-a10-v132] The Lord did not state thirteen and so on in dissolution; knowability may be a quality of being, but dissolution and non-whole remain.

[tal-a10-v133] They think not here indeed; there is no dependence on that. Let it be heard when consciousness-unity is established.

[tal-a10-v134] Consciousness is indeed even in the inert; but what question in what will be known? At the moment of self-knowledge, the dissolution-only one will be known.

[tal-a10-v135] Awakening of this is two-fold, for mantra-hood and for becoming, arising from meditation power and other Vaishnava doctrine.

[tal-a10-v136] As impressed by varied superior support, the absorbed awakened one attains mantra-hood or lordship.

[tal-a10-v137] Those devoid of freedom, subjected by delusion, awaken from dissolution, non-whole, and own impression for becoming.

[tal-a10-v138] The knowledge-particle awakens for mantra-lord or great-lord hood, or for mantra and so on, or even for worldly existence.

[tal-a10-v139] The descent differs in the state of the knower-yogi; it was said and taught by the world-lord desiring to create.

[tal-a10-v140] In the prior scripture, eight pure knowers are mentioned; therefore the teachability of which two is considered.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-śivasvācchandyamātraṃ tu bhedāyaiṣāṃ vijṛmbhate / ityāśayena saṃpaśyanviśeṣaṃ sakalādiha layākalādau novāca trāyodaśyādikaṃ vibhuḥ / nanvastu vedyatā bhāvadharmaḥ kiṃtu layākalau manvāte neha vai kiṃcittadapekṣā tvasau katham / śrūyatāṃ saṃvidaikātmyatattve@sminsaṃvyavasthite jaḍe@pi citirastyeva bhotsyamāne tu kā kathā / svabodhāvasare tāvadbhotsyate layakevalī dvividhaśca prabodho@sya mantratvāya bhavāya ca / bhāvanādibalādanyavaiṣṇavādinayoditāt yathāsvamādharauttaryavicitrātsaṃskṛtastathā / līnaḥ prabuddho mantratvaṃ tadīśatvamathaiti vā svātantryavarjitā ye tu balānmohavaśīkṛtāḥ / layākalātsvasaṃskārātprabuddhyante bhavāya te jñānākalo@pi mantreśamaheśatvāya budhyate / mantrāditvāya vā jātu jātu saṃsṛtaye@pi vā avatāro hi vijñāniyogibhāve@sya bhidyate / uktaṃ ca bodhayāmāsa sa sisṛkṣurjagatprabhuḥ vijñānakevalānaṣṭāviti śrīpūrvaśāsane / ataḥ prabhotsyamānatve yānayorbodhayogyatā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v141] By that power, fitness to be known arises here; for even in deep sleep, an unexpected arrival may come to the beloved.

[tal-a10-v142] She will see me, not in her own limbs; thus Shiva too thinks of this knowability.

[tal-a10-v143] When one will go and I create, then fitness alone is that knowability; the enjoyership of that being is so much.

[tal-a10-v144] The enjoyment of one in dissolution is wonderful; by whom is it imagined? As awareness itself is that enjoyment, manifest and manifest.

[tal-a10-v145] Even one capable of memory does not abandon the enjoyable state, though deeply asleep and bewildered, while the beloved's embraced body remains.

[tal-a10-v146] He is called the enjoyer, and he thinks enjoyership, even lacking mere imagination, before some woman of a clan.

[tal-a10-v147] Seeing a woman to be enjoyed, he rushes to delight; seeing her then, even one sharing the same intention does so.

[tal-a10-v148] Otherwise another is not found in consciousness; what do we perceive here in the world? This established thing has vision as its intermediary cause.

[tal-a10-v149] One seems pleased as if immersed, another as if extinguished while debating; thus the difference of truth is extensively illustrated.

[tal-a10-v150] From mutual difference of power and possessor, and among those made, difference arises thus with other principles.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tadbalādvedyatāyogyabhāvenaivātra vedyatā / tathāhi gāḍhanidre@pi priye@nāśaṅkitāgatām māṃ drakṣyatīti nāṅgeṣu sveṣu mātyabhisārikā / evaṃ śivo@pi manute etasyaitatpravedyatām yāsyatīti sṛjāmīti tadānīṃ yogyataiva sā / vedyatā tasya bhāvasya bhoktṛtā tāvatī ca sā layākalasya citro hi bhogaḥ kena vikalpyate / yathā yathā hi samvittiḥ sa hi bhogaḥ sphuṭo@sphuṭaḥ smṛtiyogyo@pyanyathā vā bhogyabhāvaṃ na tūjjhati / gāḍhanidrāvimūḍho@pi kāntāliṅgitavigrahaḥ bhoktaiva bhaṇyate so@pi manute bhoktṛtāṃ purā / utprekṣāmātrahīno@pi kāṃcitkulavadhūṃ puraḥ saṃbhokṣyamāṇāṃ dṛṣṭvaiva rabhasādyāti saṃmadam / tāmeva dṛṣṭvā ca tadā samānāśayabhāgapi anyastathā na saṃvitte kamatropalabhāmahe / loke rūḍhamidaṃ dṛṣṭirasminkāraṇamantarā prasīdatīva magneva nirvātīvetivādini / itthaṃ vistaratastattvabhedo@yaṃ samudāhṛtaḥ śaktiśaktimatāṃ bhedādanyonyaṃ tatkṛteṣvapi / bhedeṣvanyonyato bhedāttathā tattvāntaraiḥ saha

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v151] For one counting differences and subdifferences there is no limit anywhere; therefore this varied world-arrangement is established.

[tal-a10-v152] Even in earthliness there is no equality between Rudra and Vishnu worlds; what talk of equality elsewhere, in enjoyment or in own form?

[tal-a10-v153] That detail is not directly speakable, although it cannot be spoken; nevertheless, being told by path only, let it be distinguished.

[tal-a10-v154] When the seven mother-powers divide mutually, the form is forty-nine and more.

[tal-a10-v155] All is all-souled; therefore all powers of dissolution, art, and so on truly originate in the mother.

[tal-a10-v156] Let that unclear portion be; the lord may give it, for among them and their mutual differences there is much difference.

[tal-a10-v157] When principal differences are distinguished by water and similar elements, infinite rule variety is stated in the mode of principal difference.

[tal-a10-v158] The arisen and subordinated powers of the whole clearly extend another difference.

[tal-a10-v159] Thus another difference arises for dissolution powers and the like from impression, skill, or decay.

[tal-a10-v160] When one knows without entering the state of a subordinated power, another knowability indeed exists there.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-bhedopabhedagaṇanāṃ karvato nāvadhiḥ kvacit / tata eva vicitro@yaṃ bhuvanādividhiḥ sthitaḥ pārthivatve@pi no sāmyaṃ rudravaiṣṇavalokayoḥ / kā kathānyatra tu bhavedbhoge vāpi svarūpake sa ca no vistaraḥ sākṣācchakyo yadyapi bhāṣitum / tathāpi mārgamātreṇa kathyamāno vivicyatām saptānāṃ mātṛśaktīnāmanyonyaṃ bhedane sati / rūpamekānnapañcāśatsvarūpaṃ cādhikaṃ tataḥ sarvaṃ sarvātmakaṃ yasmāttasmātsakalamātari / layākalādiśaktīnāṃ saṃbhavo@styeva tattvataḥ sa tvasphuṭo@stu bhedāṃśaṃ dātuṃ tāvatprabhurbhavet / teṣāmapi ca bhedānāmanyonyaṃ bahubhedatā mukhyānāṃ bhedabhedānāṃ jalādyairbhedane sati / mukhyabhedaprakāreṇa vidherānantyamucyate sakalasya samudbhūtāścakṣurādisvaśaktayaḥ / nyagbhūtāśca pratanvanti bhedāntaramapi sphuṭam evaṃ layākalādīnāṃ tatsaṃskārapadoditāt / pāṭavātprakṣayādvāpi bhedāntaramudīyate nyakkṛtāṃ śaktimāsthāyāpyudāsīnatayā sthitim / anāviśyeva yadvetti tatrānyā vedyatā khalu

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v161] For a knower, through entering, immersing, expanding, and revolving, another knowability difference suitable to action arises.

[tal-a10-v162] When another power is concealed and some power clearly rises, another difference is to be known, like the view of a lute player.

[tal-a10-v163] Concealment and arising of power, from within another power and from being known or unknown, extend much difference.

[tal-a10-v164] Thus for earth and other principles, in whatever state exists, even that called pot, difference is shown there.

[tal-a10-v165] Here also knowability is called identity with knowers; therefore the pot, all-knowable, is indeed whole.

[tal-a10-v166] As long as that is knowable by Shiva alone, Shiva indeed appears; for knowledge shines one-bodied to that extent.

[tal-a10-v167] Now here the wholeness of all earth principle is shown, indeed as previously stated fifteen-fold.

[tal-a10-v168] The light that shines by non-difference of earth principle is indeed Shiva lord here; earth and Brahman is that opinion.

[tal-a10-v169] By Shiva's will, mantra great lords impel those striving to bestow powers dwelling in the earth principle.

[tal-a10-v170] Impelled mantra lords, expressers of mantras, clearly practice yoga dwelling in the earth principle by Shiva knowledge.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-āviśyeva nimajjyeva vikāsyeva vighūrṇya ca / vidato vedyatānyaiva bhedo@trārthakriyocitaḥ anyaśaktitirobhāve kasyāścitsusphuṭodaye / bhedāntaramapi jñeyaṃ vīṇāvādakadṛṣṭivat tirobhāvodbhavau śakteḥ svaśaktyantarato@nyataḥ / cetyamānādacetyādvā tanvāte bahubhedatām evametaddharādīnāṃ tattvānāṃ yāvatī daśā / kācidasti ghaṭākhyāpi tatra saṃdarśitā bhidaḥ atrāpi vedyatā nāma tādātmyaṃ vedakaiḥ saha / tataḥ sakalavedyo@sau ghaṭaḥ sakala eva hi yāvacchivaikavedyo@sau śiva evāvabhāsate / tāvadekaśarīro hi bodho bhātyeva yāvatā adhunātra samastasya dharātattvasya darśyate / sāmastya evābhihitaṃ pāñcadaśyaṃ puroditam dharātattvāvibhedena yaḥ prakāśaḥ prakāśate / sa eva śivanātho@tra pṛthivī brahma tanmatam dharātattvagatāḥ siddhīrvitarītuṃ samudyatān / prerayanti śivecchāto ye te mantramaheśvarāḥ preryamāṇāstu mantreśā mantrāstadvācakāḥ sphuṭam / dharātattvagataṃ yogamabhyasya śivavidyayā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v171] But bonded samkhya, vaishnava, and similar types, not reaching the eternal abode, enjoy the limited state of knowledge.

[tal-a10-v172] Those who, by enjoyment of principles, go to dissolution at kalpa end, endowed with deep sleep state, become pure dissolution beings.

[tal-a10-v173] In deep sleep, absorption into principle is clearly seen; otherwise, how would fixed dream vision arise?

[tal-a10-v174] Deep sleep also appears variegated, with clear and unclear states, from seeing memory variety such as 'I slept happily'.

[tal-a10-v175] When he awakens for a subtle moment from sleep, then memory is said to arise; memory is not born from object-born knowledge.

[tal-a10-v176] Therefore, what fools say—that memory of cotton and pleasant touch arises between awakenings—is untenable.

[tal-a10-v177] Here all persons to be known are earth-ascending, free from impurity mixed with great karma excitement.

[tal-a10-v178] The agitation in planning own activities of this sevenfold is that which is clearly said of the sevenfold powers.

[tal-a10-v179] Shiva, indeed imperishable consciousness form, has three powers; those are conditioned by autonomy into grasper form.

[tal-a10-v180] Mantra endings would stand threefold, indifferent like, due to object form coloring and grasper form condition.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-na tu pāśavasāṃkhyīyavaiṣṇavādidvitādṛśā / aprāptadhruvadhāmāno vijñānākalatājuṣaḥ tāvattattvopabhogena ye kalpānte layaṃ gatāḥ / sauṣuptāvasthayopetāste@tra pralayakevalāḥ sauṣupte tattvalīnatvaṃ sphuṭameva hi lakṣyate / anyathā niyatasvapnasaṃdṛṣṭirjāyate kutaḥ sauṣuptamapi citraṃ ca svacchāsvacchādi bhāsate / asvāpsaṃ sukhamityādismṛtivaicitryadarśanāt yadaiva sa kṣaṇaṃ sūkṣmaṃ nidrāyaiva prabuddhyate / tadaiva smṛtireṣeti nārthajajñānajā smṛtiḥ tena mūḍhairyaducyeta prabuddhasyāntarāntarā / tūlikādisukhasparśasmṛtireṣeti tatkutaḥ māhākarmasamullāsasaṃmiśritamalābilāḥ / dharādhirohiṇo jñeyāḥ sakalā iha pudgalāḥ asyaiva saptakasya svasvavyāpāraprakalpane / prakṣobho yastadevoktaṃ śaktīnāṃ saptakaṃ sphuṭam śivo hyacyutacidrūpastisrastacchaktayastu yāḥ / tāḥ svātantryavaśopāttagrahītrākāratāvaśāt tridhā mantrāvasānāḥ syurudāsīnā iva sthitāḥ / grāhyākāroparāgāttu grahītrākāratāvaśāt

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v181] The three powers, will, knowledge, and action, are considered; sevenfold knowerhood arises thus from its agitation and measurehood.

[tal-a10-v182] But that which is pure and inert, devoid of grasper, form, consciousness, and contact, is the universe's nature, threefold.

[tal-a10-v183] Thus even water and the rest would be said divided by differences; by this direction, mostly, it is found in all differences.

[tal-a10-v184] This difference among mantra great lords is fifteenfold; nevertheless, because it lacks clarity, even though existing, it is not discussed.

[tal-a10-v185] And this is summarized by the creator in the previous Sri, which indeed says, by lordship with activity and so on, the waking state and so forth.

[tal-a10-v186] Even in undivided Shiva, according to the subtle knowledge within, now in the prana-shakti-established net of principles, it is distinguished.

[tal-a10-v187] This difference, as fifteenfold and so on, Sri Shambhu taught; in all meaning here, in the ungraspable, there are sixteen moment-sparks.

[tal-a10-v188] In the movement of thirty-six angulas, conceived as half and quarter angulas, the first there is supreme nondual, essence of undivided taste.

[tal-a10-v189] The second is the form of grasper expansion, manifested; but the last has become self-nature by identity with graspedness.

[tal-a10-v190] Indeed the penultimate grasper moment is not to be separately manifested; but from the third moment, six moments are established.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sakalāntāstu tāstisra icchājñānakriyā matāḥ / saptadhetthaṃ pramātṛtvaṃ tatkṣobho mānatā tathā yattu grahītṛtārūpasaṃvitsaṃsparśavarjitam / śuddhaṃ jaḍaṃ tatsvarūpamitthaṃ viśvaṃ trikātmakam evaṃ jalādyapi vadedbhedairbhinnaṃ mahāmatiḥ / anayā tu diśā prāyaḥ sarvabhedeṣu vidyate bhedo mantramaheśānteṣveṣa pañcadaśātmakaḥ / tathāpi sphuṭatābhāvātsannapyeṣa na carcitaḥ etacca sūtritaṃ dhātrā śrīpūrve yadbravīti hi / savyāpārādhipatvenetyādinā jāgradāditām abhinne@pi śive@ntaḥsthasūkṣmabodhānusārataḥ / adhunā prāṇaśaktisthe tattvajāle vivicyate bhedo@yaṃ pāñcadaśyādiryathā śrīśaṃbhurādiśat / samaste@rthe@tra nirgrāhye tuṭayaḥ ṣoḍaśa kṣaṇāḥ ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgule cāre sāṃśadvyaṅgulakalpitāḥ / tatrādyaḥ paramādvaito nirvibhāgarasātmakaḥ dvitīyo grāhakollāsarūpaḥ prativibhāvyate / antyastu grāhyatādātmyātsvarūpībhāvamāgataḥ pravibhāvyo na hi pṛthagupāntyo grāhakaḥ kṣaṇaḥ / tṛtīyaṃ kṣaṇamārabhya kṣaṇaṣaṭkaṃ tu yatsthitam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v191] That nondiscursive state, consisting of rising discursive covering, that itself is known as Shiva's form, consisting of supreme power.

[tal-a10-v192] The second, middle, sixfold consists of supreme and lower levels; this discursive rise too has gone to gradual clarity.

[tal-a10-v193] In the first hexad here, the three goddesses, touching opening and closing modes quickly, attain a sixfold state.

[tal-a10-v194] Thus in the second hexad too, what? Here, having reached the eclipse state by the object path, they stand as supreme and lower.

[tal-a10-v195] In the first hexad here, those goddesses, from freedom's exuberance alone, even in desired conditioning, would remain not fallen from supreme form.

[tal-a10-v196] There is also some excellence among them, increasing progressively, which is shown by wise possessors of discernment even after making it clear.

[tal-a10-v197] Some, placing one pulse in the object and one also in the subject by identity, know a sevenfold and a sevenfold.

[tal-a10-v198] Striving for measuring in that subtle awareness, they experience what form there; what use are speech boasts?

[tal-a10-v199] Thus the process from earth to root end, going by life breath, is taught by guru lineage order in difference, fifteenfold.

[tal-a10-v200] But by order, in lesser difference, deficiency would be even in pulses; in that, conceptualization decreases and clarity of the non-conceptual increases.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tannirvikalpaṃ prodgacchadvikalpācchādanātmakam / tadeva śivarūpaṃ hi paraśaktyātmakaṃ viduḥ dvitīyaṃ madhyamaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ parāparapadātmakam / vikalparūḍhirapyeṣā kramātprasphuṭatāṃ gatā ṣaṭke@tra prathame devyastisraḥ pronmeṣavṛttitām / nimeṣavṛttitāṃ cāśu spṛśantyaḥ ṣaṭkatāṃ gatāḥ evaṃ dvitīyaṣaṭke@pi kiṃ tvatra grāhyavartmanā / uparāgapadaṃ prāpya parāparatayā sthitāḥ ādye@tra ṣaṭke tā devyaḥ svātantryollāsamātrataḥ / jighṛkṣite@pyupādhau syuḥ pararūpādavicyutāḥ asti cātiśayaḥ kaścittāsāmapyuttarottaram / yo vivekadhanairdhīraiḥ sphuṭīkṛtyāpi darśyate kecittvekāṃ tuṭiṃ grāhye caikāmapi grahītari / tādātmyena vinikṣipya saptakaṃ saptakaṃ viduḥ tadasyāṃ sūkṣmasaṃvittau kalanāya samudyatāḥ / saṃvedayante yadrūpaṃ tatra kiṃ vāgvikatthanaiḥ evaṃ dharādimūlāntaṃ prakriyā prāṇagāminī / guruparvakramātproktā bhede pañcadaśātmake kramāttu bhedanyūnatve nyūnatā syāttuṭiṣvapi / tasyāṃ hrāso vikalpasya sphuṭatā cāvikalpinaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v201] As indeed a long-suffering distressed person, afterward established in happiness, forgets that suffering by the path of happiness's rest.

[tal-a10-v202] So, even when conceptualization is gone, people rooted in experience do not regard that existence by the force of conceptualization's rest.

[tal-a10-v203] By decrease of conceptualization, conceptualization-barren supreme truth goes to manifestness of awareness nature; thus good intellect belongs to strivers in attention there.

[tal-a10-v204] In the connection of object and subject awareness, this attentiveness is that spoken there, all-desires-milking, because of that.

[tal-a10-v205] Thus, as duality decreases, the two tuṭis gradually and clearly go to deficiency.

[tal-a10-v206] Therefore in Śiva-entry two tuṭis are praised; but that one tuṭi there is full, pure, and alone.

[tal-a10-v208] Thus glorious Kallaṭa said: the fall of tuṭi is gain in all-knowing agency; the fall of tuṭi is the supreme tuṭi.

[tal-a10-v209] In the first tuṭi all has gone to full unity everywhere; what there is knowable, doable, or named?

[tal-a10-v210] Therefore the wise seek the initial Devī-pratibhā, blossoming with difference, for accomplishment of omniscience and so on.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yathā hi ciraduḥkhārtaḥ paścādāttasukhasthitiḥ / vismaratyeva tadduḥkhaṃ sukhaviśrāntivartmanā tathā gatavikalpe@pi rūḍhāḥ saṃvedane janāḥ / vikalpaviśrāntibalāttāṃ sattāṃ nābhimanvate vikalpanirhrāsavaśena yāti vikalpavandhyā paramārthasatyā / saṃvitsvarūpaprakaṭatvamitthaṃ tatrāvadhāne yatatāṃ subuddhiḥ grāhyagrāhakasaṃvittau saṃbandhe sāvadhānatā / iyaṃ sā tatra tatroktā sarvakāmadughā yataḥ evaṃ dvayaṃ dvayaṃ yāvannyūnībhavati bhedagam / tāvattuṭidvayaṃ yāti nyūnatāṃ kramaśaḥ sphuṭam ata eva śivāveśe dvituṭiḥ parigīyate / ekā tu sā tuṭistatra pūrṇā śuddhaiva kevalam dvitīyā śiva(śakti)rūpaiva sarvajñānakriyātmikā / tasyāmavahito yogī kiṃ na vetti karoti vā tathā coktaṃ kallaṭena śrīmatā tuṭipātagaḥ / lābhaḥ sarvajñakartṛtve tuṭeḥ pāto@parā tuṭiḥ ādyāyāṃ tu tuṭau sarvaṃ sarvataḥ pūrṇamekatām / gataṃ kiṃ tatra vedyaṃ vā kāryaṃ vā vyapadeśabhāk ato bhedasamullāsakalāṃ prāthamikīṃ budhāḥ / cinvanti pratibhāṃ devīṃ sarvajñatvādisiddhaye

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v212] In them, fixing the mind with one-pointed attention, the respective siddhi-entrance arises by itself.

[tal-a10-v213] Therefore, as multiplicity of difference is distance, so in consciousness many tuṭis are like non-contact with the desired object.

[tal-a10-v214] As tuṭis decrease, difference decreases; so consciousness becomes nearer, up to Śiva.

[tal-a10-v215] The Śiva principle is said to be near from all sides; therefore no effort is found in entering it.

[tal-a10-v216] As distance, so effort; thus meditation, action, and so on have no scope in Śiva.

[tal-a10-v217] Therefore indeed people think so, for let the world be seen as in perception of pot and so on.

[tal-a10-v218] It appears as one with effort; so what is this internality in pleasure perception? They say consciousness-nearness.

[tal-a10-v219] That consciousness-form manifestation and externality, its closing for beings, even near does not appear, so extreme distance.

[tal-a10-v220] Even far, having become near, appearance may be here; how then not like seed, sprout, vine, leaf, flower, fruit, and so on?
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-saiva śaktiḥ śivasyoktā tṛtīyādituṭiṣvatha / mantrādi(dhi)nāthatacchaktimantreśādyāḥ kramoditāḥ tāsu saṃdadhataścittamavadhānaikadharmakam / tattatsiddhisamāveśaḥ svayamevopajāyate ata eva yathā bhedabahutvaṃ dūratā tathā / saṃvittau tuṭibāhulyādakṣārthāsaṃnikarṣavat yathā yathā hi nyūnatvaṃ tuṭīnāṃ hrāsato bhidaḥ / tathā tathātinaikaṭyaṃ saṃvidaḥ syācchivāvadhi śivatattvamataḥ proktamantikaṃ sarvato@mutaḥ / ata eva prayatno@yaṃ tatpraveśe na vidyate yathā yathā hi dūratvaṃ yatnayogastathā tathā / bhāvanākaraṇādīnāṃ śive niravakāśatām ata eva hi manyante saṃpradāyadhanā janāḥ / tathā hi dṛśyatāṃ loko ghaṭādervedane yathā prayatnavānivābhāti tathā kiṃ sukhavedane / āntaratvamidaṃ prāhuḥ saṃvinnaikaṭyaśālitām tāṃ ca cidrūpatonmeṣaṃ bāhyatvaṃ tannimeṣatām / bhavināṃ tvantiko@pyevaṃ na bhātītyatidūratā dūre@pi hyantikībhūte bhānaṃ syāttvatra tatkatham / na ca bījāṅkuralatādalapuṣpaphalādivat

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v221] This sequential thing may be a consciousness thread there; indeed a sprout from seed, vine, and not a sprout from seed here from all.

[tal-a10-v222] The consciousness principle, shining and complete everywhere, is declared the cause of all, arisen everywhere, because.

[tal-a10-v223] Therefore indeed, even in the pot, if this breath function shines, it may rest quickly; there indeed it may go to dissolution in the Shiva seed.

[tal-a10-v225] And from Shiva non-difference, what then in duality from nearness perception? By this direction all is always discriminated.

[tal-a10-v226] Extended Bhairava indeed immediately has gone to consciousness-wheel lordship; thus the breath-goer difference is hidden by the Khechari wheel.

[tal-a10-v227] By me, following Shambhava command, it is revealed: in this path, knowability having been attained, consciousness may arise.

[tal-a10-v228] Of that, its own variety is called state-word: waking, dream, deep sleep, and the fourth, and beyond that.

[tal-a10-v229] Thus they say five words in one Veda; there this pathway of principles runs from earth principle to Shiva.

[tal-a10-v230] In that one knower, if necessarily, waking and the rest are shown; by Shambhunatha's grace this is known by me.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-kramikeyaṃ bhavetsaṃvitsūtastatra kilāṅkuraḥ / bījāllatā tvaṅkurānno bījādiha sarvataḥ saṃvittattvaṃ bhāsamānaṃ paripūrṇaṃ hi sarvataḥ / sarvasya kāraṇaṃ proktaṃ sarvatraivoditaṃ yataḥ tata eva ghaṭe@pyeṣā prāṇavṛttiryadi sphuret / viśrāmyeccāśu tatraiva śivabīje layaṃ vrajet na tu kramikatā kācicchivātmatve kadācana / anyanmantrādi(dhi)nāthādi kāraṇaṃ tattu saṃnidheḥ śivābhedācca kiṃ cātha dvaite naikaṭyavedanāt / anayā ca diśā sarva sarvadā pravivecayan bhairavāyata eva drāk ciccakreśvaratāṃ gataḥ / sa itthaṃ prāṇago bhedaḥ khecarīcakragopitaḥ mayā prakaṭitaḥ śrīmacchāmbhavājñānuvartinā / atraivādhvani vedyatvaṃ prāpte yā saṃvidudbhavet tasyāḥ svakaṃ yadvaicitryaṃ tadavasthāpadābhidham / jāgratsvapnaḥ suṣuptaṃ ca turyaṃ ca tadatītakam iti pañca padānyāhurekasminvedake sati / tatra yaiṣā dharātattvācchivāntā tattvapaddhatiḥ tasyāmekaḥ pramātā cedavaśyaṃ jāgradādikam / taddarśyate śaṃbhunāthaprasādādviditaṃ mayā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v231] What is to be superintended only here is never the superintender; the known object in experience is called waking.

[tal-a10-v232] Things like Chaitra and Maitra are principles from earth; words become means of denotation; what? denotation too is cognition.

[tal-a10-v233] The fourfold of knower, known, means of knowledge, and cognition; this universe is to be superintended; when waking, then it is remembered.

[tal-a10-v234] For thus appears that blue within in cognition of thought-form; of the external, its superintender is the cognizer.

[tal-a10-v235] But that blue shines as external; for him no superintender-state exists in any way; that is called waking.

[tal-a10-v236] There in appearing Chaitra, the body-part is called unawakened; the cognition-part is awakened and is the cognition-maker.

[tal-a10-v237] Awakened, fully awakened, and cognition-only etc. form a sequence; fourfold indeed in bodily waking is proclaimed.

[tal-a10-v238] Waking and the rest fourfold indeed exists each here; waking-waking-unawakened is that; waking-dream is awakenedness.

[tal-a10-v239] Etc.; beyond-fourth however, because all-pervading, how separate? Also bodily waking-unawakened and awakened only are said.

[tal-a10-v240] Awakened, fully awakened, fourfold this is remembered; this object-ground is primary; waking-named, other intermediate.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yadadhiṣṭheyameveha nādhiṣṭhātṛ kadācana / saṃvedanagataṃ vedyaṃ tajjāgratsamudāhṛtam caitramaitrādibhūtāni tattvāni ca dharāditaḥ / abhidhākaraṇībhūtāḥ śabdāḥ kiṃ cābhidhā pramā pramātṛmeyatanmānapramārūpaṃ catuṣṭayam / viśvametadadhiṣṭheyaṃ yadā jāgrattadā smṛtam tathā hi bhāsate yattannīlamantaḥ pravedane / saṃkalparūpe bāhyasya tadadhiṣṭhātṛ bodhakam yattu bāhyatayā nīlaṃ cakāstyasya na vidyate / kathaṃcidapyadhiṣṭhātṛbhāvastajjāgraducyate tatra caitre bhāsamāne yo dehāṃśaḥ sa kathyate / abuddho yastu mānāṃśaḥ sa buddho mitikārakaḥ prabuddhaḥ suprabuddhaśca pramāmātreti ca kramaḥ / cāturvidhyaṃ hi piṇḍasthanāmni jāgrati kīrtitam jāgradādi catuṣkaṃ hi pratyekamiha vidyate / jāgrajjāgradabuddhaṃ tajjāgratsvapnastu buddhatā ityādi turyātītaṃ tu sarvagatvātpṛthakkutaḥ / uktaṃ ca piṇḍagaṃ jāgradabuddhaṃ buddhameva ca prabuddhaṃ suprabuddhaṃ ca caturvidhamidaṃ smṛtam / meyabhūmiriyaṃ mukhyā jāgradākhyānyadantarā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v241] In the Shri Malini view, the presided-over element principle is called body-located.

[tal-a10-v242] The worldly waking state is also called body-located, defined for yogis' accomplishment of yoga.

[tal-a10-v243] The identity of a yogi seated in presided samadhi is body-located, measured and condensed.

[tal-a10-v244] For knowers established in discrimination, that is called all-around auspicious full by object existence.

[tal-a10-v245] Because the knower sees the universe full of all existence, its consciousness-nature shines.

[tal-a10-v246] Because of the triple form of world, yoga, and discrimination, three names are spoken; the same rule applies in dreams.

[tal-a10-v247] The knowable remains, previously described as real and element-principle-named, when superimposed on the presiding instrument state.

[tal-a10-v248] That dream is primarily to be known, since it appears similar to a knowable on an imaginary path.

[tal-a10-v249] The worldly-established dream has similarity and lacks external form in visions like imagination, dream, intention, memory, and madness.

[tal-a10-v250] The clear knowable is waking-primary; what is unclear there appears with a clear presider.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-bhūtatattvābhidhānānāṃ yoṃ@śo@dhiṣṭheya ucyate / piṇḍasthamiti taṃ prāhuriti śrīmālinīmate laukikī jāgradityeṣā saṃjñā piṇḍasthamityapi / yogināṃ yogasiddhyarthaṃ saṃjñeyaṃ paribhāṣyate adhiṣṭheyasamāpattimadhyāsīnasya yoginaḥ / tādātmyaṃ kila piṇḍasthaṃ mitaṃ piṇḍaṃ hi piṇḍitam prasaṃkhyānaikarūḍhānāṃ jñānināṃ tu taducyate / sarvatobhadramāpūrṇaṃ sarvato vedyasattayā sarvasattāsamāpūrṇa viśvaṃ paśyedyato yataḥ / jñānī tatastataḥ saṃvittatvamasya prakāśate lokayogaprasaṃkhyānatrairūpyavaśataḥ kila / nāmāni trīṇi bhaṇyante svapnādiṣvapyayaṃ vidhiḥ yattvadhiṣṭhānakaraṇabhāvamadhyāsya vartate / vedyaṃ satpūrvakathitaṃ bhūtatattvābhidhāmayam tatsvapno mukhyato jñeyaṃ tacca vaikalpike pathi / vaikalpikapathārūḍhavedyasāmyāvabhāsanāt lokarūḍho@pyasau svapnaḥ sāmyaṃ cābāhyarūpatā / utprekṣāsvapnasaṃkalpasmṛtyunmādādidṛṣṭiṣu vispaṣṭaṃ yadvedyajātaṃ jāgranmukhyatayaiva tat / yattu tatrāpyavispaṣṭaṃ spaṣṭādhiṣṭhātṛ bhāsate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v251] A knowable gone to another imagination is called a dream state; then it knows its own lack of externality.

[tal-a10-v252] There also, in that unsteady selfhood, one should imagine the fourfoldness as before.

[tal-a10-v253] Coming and going, well-scattered, gathered, well-composed; here too the worldly name dream is thus this.

[tal-a10-v254] Sleep is considered non-grasping of desired external states; it is a state of all paths, with life-breath and thought of going.

[tal-a10-v255] Yogis know absorption in that state and the existence of the knowable, without considering the external, everywhere.

[tal-a10-v256] In the knowable, a portion of freedom; knowledge may share dream by pervasion; this measure-ground is primary, and dream is of the nature of reflection.

[tal-a10-v257] The reflection of the knowable is indeed called the support of the measurable, from the support-base of the previously said permanent body.

[tal-a10-v258] The seed of the universe, that silent, is called deep sleep; in experience and imagination, that seer is indeed he.

[tal-a10-v259] Deep sleep is called sleep because it resembles ordinary sleep, though being is not grasped there.

[tal-a10-v260] The primary mother state, with seed-being and silent nature, is declared deep sleep.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-vikalpāntaragaṃ vedyaṃ tatsvapnapadamucyate / tadaiva tasya vettyeva svayameva hyabāhyatām pramātrantarasādhārabhāvahānyasthirātmate / tatrāpi cāturvidhyaṃ tat prāgdiśaiva prakalpayet gatāgataṃ suvikṣiptaṃ saṃgataṃ susamāhitam / atrāpi pūrvavannāma laukikaṃ svapna ityadaḥ bāhyābhimatabhāvānāṃ svāpo hyagrahaṇaṃ matam / sarvādhvanaḥ padaṃ prāṇaḥ saṃkalpo@vagamātmakaḥ padaṃ ca tatsamāpatti padasthaṃ yogino viduḥ / vedyasattāṃ bahirbhūtāmanapekṣyaiva sarvataḥ vedye svātantryabhāg jñānaṃ svapnaṃ vyāptitayā bhajet / mānabhūmiriyaṃ mukhyā svapno hyāmarśanātmakaḥ vedyacchāyo@vabhāso hi meye@dhiṣṭhānamucyate / yattvadhiṣṭhātṛbhūtādeḥ pūrvoktasya vapurdhruvam bījaṃ viśvasya tattūṣṇīṃbhūtaṃ sauṣuptamucyate / anubhūtau vikalpe ca yo@sau draṣṭā sa eva hi na bhāvagrahaṇaṃ tena suṣṭhu suptatvamucyate / tatsāmyāllaukikīṃ nidrāṃ suṣuptaṃ manvate budhāḥ bījabhāvo@thāgrahaṇaṃ sāmyaṃ tūṣṇīṃsvabhāvatā / mukhyā mātṛdaśā seyaṃ suṣuptākhyā nigadyate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v261] Yogis know indifference through absorption while abiding in form.

[tal-a10-v262] Great pervasion follows because a contraction of the knowable is absent.

[tal-a10-v263] Even for the indifferent one, the knowable is fourfold through superimposition on elements.

[tal-a10-v264] A vast, peaceful, clear cognition-natured form stands upon the knower.

[tal-a10-v265] The fourth state is the absorption of power, reached by falling away from fullness, aim, and indifference.

[tal-a10-v266] Some call consciousness self-luminous; it is distinct from object, means, and knower, because the triad exists for that purpose.

[tal-a10-v267] Object, means, and knower form the triad; he too rests clearly in that measurement, and that goddess is the life of the whole world.

[tal-a10-v268] Transcending form, seeing, and I, one abides; relying on door-only means and seeing without means.

[tal-a10-v269] Knowerhood, whose nature is freedom, shines as the fourth form of consciousness; itself light, that is it.

[tal-a10-v270] In absorption identity knowerhood becomes clear; from absorption coloring meanshood arises, and objecthood again.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-rūpakatvācca rūpaṃ tattādātmyaṃ yoginaḥ punaḥ / rūpasthaṃ tatsamāpattyaudāsīnyaṃ rūpiṇāṃ viduḥ prasaṃkhyānavataḥ kāpi vedyasaṃkocanātra yat / nāsti tena mahāvyāptiriyaṃ tadanusārataḥ udāsīnasya tasyāpi vedyaṃ yena caturvidham / bhūtādi tadupādhyutthamatra bhedacatuṣṭayam uditaṃ vipulaṃ śāntaṃ suprasannamathāparam / yattu pramātmakaṃ rūpaṃ pramāturupari sthitam pūrṇatāgamanaunmukhyamaudāsīnyātparicyutiḥ / tatturyamucyate śaktisamāveśo hyasau mataḥ sā saṃvitsvaprakāśā tu kaiściduktā prameyataḥ / mānānmātuśca bhinnaiva tadarthaṃ tritayaṃ yataḥ meyaṃ māne mātari tat so@pi tasyāṃ mitau sphuṭam / viśrāmyatīti saivaiṣā devī viśvaikajīvitam rūpaṃ dṛśāhamityaṃśatrayamuttīrya vartate / dvāramātrāśritopāyā paśyāmītyanupāyikā pramātṛtā svatantratvarūpā seyaṃ prakāśate / saṃvitturīyarūpaivaṃ prakāśātmā svayaṃ ca sā tatsamāveśatādātmye mātṛtvaṃ bhavati sphuṭam / tatsamāveśoparāgānmānatvaṃ meyatā punaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v271] From absorption proximity, that grace, and dissolution of object difference, that diseaseless state is said.

[tal-a10-v273] Other and higher-lower are twofold; that is higher, but this, fallen from formality and indifference, turns toward fullness.

[tal-a10-v274] In that state there is absorption; the yogi, through fullness-aim yoga, sees the universe beyond form and becomes full of that.

[tal-a10-v275] Well-counted accumulation is held; in this, no other fourth state is possible indeed.

[tal-a10-v276] Consciousness indeed shines as object by knowing only; waking and other prior states are possible for her, because.

[tal-a10-v277] By threefold grace this is said in trika teaching: manonmana is infinite and all-purpose by distinction.

[tal-a10-v278] But that full unlimited bliss-laden beyond-fourth they call that same supreme state.

[tal-a10-v279] Here yoga has no real existence because meditation is absent; in the independent immeasurable state, meditatability is nowhere.

[tal-a10-v280] Because yoga and the rest are absent, no name is given to the lord in this; by power of distinction this form is by fullness union.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tatsamāveśanaikaṭyāttrayaṃ tattadanugrahāt / vedyādibhedagalanāduktā seyamanāmayā mātrādyanugrahādā(dhā)nātsavyāpāreti bhaṇyate / jāgradādyapi devasya śaktitvena vyavasthitam aparaṃ parāparaṃ ca dvidhā tatsā parā tviyam / rūpakatvādudāsīnāccyuteyaṃ pūrṇatonmukhī daśā tasyāṃ samāpattī rūpātītaṃ tu yoginaḥ / pūrṇataunmukhyayogitvādviśvaṃ paśyati tanmayaḥ prasaṃkhyātā pracayatasteneyaṃ pracayo matā / naitasyāmaparā turyadaśā saṃbhāvyate kila saṃvinna kila vedyā sā vittvenaiva hi bhāsate / jāgradādyāstu saṃbhāvyāstisro@syāḥ prāgdaśā yataḥ tritayānugrahātseyaṃ tenoktā trikaśāsane / manonmanamanantaṃ ca sarvārthamiti bhedataḥ yattu pūrṇānavacchinnavapurānandanirbharam / turyātītaṃ tu tatprāhustadeva paramaṃ padam nātra yogasya sadbhāvo bhāvanāderabhāvataḥ / aprameye@paricchinne svatantre bhāvyatā kutaḥ yogādyabhāvatastena nāmāsminnādiśadvibhuḥ / prasaṃkhyānabalāttvetadrūpaṃ pūrṇatvayogataḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v281] Here anuttara is said, called great accumulation; from fullness only, possibility of differences in this is not indeed.

[tal-a10-v282] For refuting that, difference is not said as qualifier in this; ever-risen thus indicates all-pervasion.

[tal-a10-v283] Indeed difference never becomes one anywhere; in beyond-fourth, difference one ever-risen thus this.

[tal-a10-v284] Therefore foolish doctrine; nondifference of this is established, but in holy previous scripture by him said, knowers understand other state-standing.

[tal-a10-v285] Mantras and their lords with remainder are praised as form-standing; beyond form supreme power acts without disease.

[tal-a10-v286] Pure shiva beyond all, established in own self, is to be known; having known him one is liberated.

[tal-a10-v287] Thus holy shambhunatha represented real existence in waking and so on.

[tal-a10-v288] But others speak another mode resorted; the form of waking and so on is now examined.

[tal-a10-v289] Waking perception arises through sense activity and repeatedly grasps external forms.

[tal-a10-v290] Dream is self-created imagination, opposite to waking, conditioned by impurity and action.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v291] Deep sleep becomes stable through night absence and limited enjoyment.

[tal-a10-v292] Three powers remain situated in the fourth state.

[tal-a10-v293] Beings become self-nondual as they enter bhairava knowledge.

[tal-a10-v294] In the beyond-fourth state, clear form is considered waking.

[tal-a10-v295] Unstable appearances are dream, unclear ones are sleep.

[tal-a10-v296] The fourth state is a thread-like continuity grasped in all differences.

[tal-a10-v297] Beyond the fourth state is nondual joy that melts all difference.

[tal-a10-v298] The wise follow all states in order everywhere.

[tal-a10-v299] In the full lord, consciousness beyond the fourth is named.

[tal-a10-v300] Knowledge power is dream and action power is waking in reality.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a10-v301] The great lord clearly stated this primacy in the earlier treatise.

[tal-a10-v302] The waking state consists of own form, power, and whole in fifteenfold difference.

[tal-a10-v303] Beyond the fourth, power and Shambhu belong to dream and deep sleep in thirteenfold form.

[tal-a10-v304] Own form appears apart from waking as before, with two in waking-dream-sleep and fourth as before.

[tal-a10-v305] Five waking states arise, including mantras, leaders, lords, power, and Shambhu.

[tal-a10-v306] In sevenfold mantra distinction, five states are named as waking and so forth.

[tal-a10-v307] The essential nature is the five powers in the mantra-lord, in fivefold division.

[tal-a10-v308] Own action, knowledge, will, Shambhu, and the fifth are established in the threefold division of the great lord, including waking and the rest.

[tal-a10-v309] Through activity, lordship, abundance, impelling, cessation of will, and abiding in his own state, Shiva, though one, is fivefold.

[tal-a10-v310] Thus this tattva path has been shown by us in detail, and then...
